chapter.title: Processes
chapter.para: A process (in ARINC 653 terms; thread in the code) is the unit of execution inside a partition. The names of the services follow ARINC 653. The scheduling of the partitions is in the chapter "Scheduling".

section.para: JetOS shall create a process of a partition only while the partition is not in NORMAL mode, with the attributes given: its name, entry point, base priority, period, time capacity, deadline and stack size.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: All processes exist when the partition starts to work normally.

section.para: JetOS shall refuse with an error a request to create a process with an invalid attribute, a name that another process of the partition has, or an entry point outside executable code.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A process must not start with attributes that the kernel cannot honour.

section.para: JetOS shall accept base and current priorities only from 1 to 239.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: This is the range of priorities of the processes of a partition.

section.para: JetOS shall give, on request, the identifier of a process identified by its name, and the name, entry point, attributes, current priority and state of a process identified by its identifier.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Processes are found by name and then controlled by identifier.

section.para: JetOS shall not find the main process and the error handler by name.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The main process and the error handler are not processes that the application created.

section.para: JetOS shall run in a partition, among its ready processes, the one with the highest current priority, and among those of the same priority the one that has been ready for longest.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: This is the ARINC 653 scheduling of processes.

section.para: JetOS shall preempt the running process as soon as a process of a higher priority becomes ready, unless the partition has locked preemption.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A higher-priority process responds without delay.

section.para: JetOS shall let a process wait for a duration or until a time, yield to the ready processes of its priority, suspend itself with a time-out or without, and end its own activation.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: These are the services of a process to give the processor away.

section.para: JetOS shall make a process that waits for a duration of zero yield to the ready processes of its priority.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: These are the services of a process to give the processor away.

section.para: JetOS shall do nothing for a suspension of a process with a time-out of zero.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: These are the services of a process to give the processor away.

section.para: JetOS shall refuse a request for a process to wait, with an error, while the partition is locked, is not in NORMAL mode, or the process is the error handler.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A wait there would block the partition.

section.para: JetOS shall let a process suspend another process of the partition, and resume a suspended process.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: ARINC 653 lets a process control another one.

section.para: JetOS shall keep a suspended process waiting, without running it, until it is resumed.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: ARINC 653 lets a process control another one.

section.para: JetOS shall let a process start a stopped process after a delay (none for an immediate start) and stop another process or itself.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: ARINC 653 lets a process control the life of another one.

section.para: JetOS shall run a stopped process again only after it is started.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Stopping a process inside a critical section would leave the section locked for ever.

section.para: JetOS shall stop a process that is in a critical section only after it has left the section.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Stopping a process inside a critical section would leave the section locked for ever.

section.para: JetOS shall let a process change the current priority of a process.
JetOS shall put a process whose current priority is changed after the ready processes of its new priority.
JetOS shall, at the end of an activation of a periodic process, hold the process until its next activation and move its deadline to match the new activation.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: These are the periodic wait and the replenishment of ARINC 653.

section.para: JetOS shall let a process move its own deadline to a time that is the present time plus a budget, an infinite budget removing the deadline of an aperiodic process.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: These are the periodic wait and the replenishment of ARINC 653.

section.para: JetOS shall raise a deadline missed error of a process (see health monitoring) when the process has not ended its activation before its deadline.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The health monitoring is the means to recover from a late process.

section.para: JetOS shall keep a context of its own for each process: a kernel stack, a user stack, the registers, and the state of the floating point unit.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A process must not see the effect of the others on its registers.

section.para: JetOS shall restore the context of a process when the process runs again.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A process must not see the effect of the others on its registers.

section.para: JetOS shall never let a process or a partition see the floating point state of another process.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The floating point registers may hold data of another partition.
